name: Common Deletion--Link Form of a Peripheral Daisy Obstruction
statement: In a reduced-root peripheral obstruction $C(K,L,P)$, put $N=E\setminus P$. There is one set $A\subseteq N$ such that for every $p\in P$, the deletion--link differences are singletons $\Delta_p(K)=\{(P\setminus\{p\})\cup A\}$ and $\Delta_p(L)=\{(P\setminus\{p\})\cup(N\setminus A)\}$. Thus every incompatible root coordinate sees the same complementary outside part.
proof: Minimality makes every old-coordinate restriction and contraction root-compatible. For each $p$, these constraints fix every other coordinate on both nonempty deletion--link differences, with all other root coordinates equal to one and the outside coordinates complementary, so both differences are singletons. Comparing the top $P$-sections of the down-set $K$ then forces the outside singleton part to be independent of $p$.
